subject: HelioTech pricing alignment: incentive schedule vs SKU repack
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ava Morgan <ava@heliotech.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HelioTech pricing alignment: incentive schedule vs SKU repack

Hi Ava — great to connect earlier. As discussed, we ran two structured incentive approaches that map to the migration paths HelioTech outlined. I attached a short spreadsheet with example math for both: helio-incentive-options.xlsx.

Short summary of the two paths we think are most realistic:

1) Timed/stepped credits (fast onramp):
- 9-month stepped credit pool that scales with usage ramp (months 1-3: 40% credit on incremental tokens; months 4-6: 25%; months 7-9: 10%)
- Good if you want near-term TCO parity while minimizing long-term price reduction

2) Volume-tier tariff (commit + SKU repack):
- 18% baseline discount at 12-month commit; additional % increase at defined volume thresholds (250M, 500M tokens)
- SKU repack: map HelioTech/CurrentVendor SKU usage to Redwood unit bundles to preserve billing predictability

We think the timed-credit option is lower risk for Redwood while giving HelioTech faster realized savings during migration. The volume-tier with SKU repack is simpler for procurement and gives better longterm unit economics if volume hits the higher thresholds.

Requested next steps:
- Which of the two you want us to formalize into a term sheet (I can send a DocuSign-ready option)?
- If procurement needs a fixed example quote, tell me the target committed spend (monthly or annual) and we’ll produce a formal CMA.

Attachments: helio-incentive-options.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min call with procurement tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Karthik	
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0142

From: Ava Morgan <ava@heliotech.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@heliotech.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HelioTech pricing alignment: incentive schedule vs SKU repack

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet. A few quick clarifications from procurement before we escalate:

- Procurement prefers a single signed term with clearly enumerated credits rather than ongoing per-token credits that look variable. Can you provide a contractual illustration for the timed-credit option that lists maximum credit amounts and how they apply to invoices?
- For the SKU repack: we need a sample mapping from our current vendor SKUs to Redwood bundles because our billing team will only accept a clear 1:1 mapping in the contract.
- We’re also evaluating whether to ask for a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration engineering cost — can you provide a range you’d be willing to offer (ballpark $20k–$50k)?

Our procurement timeline: we aim to finalize vendor selection by Friday 2027-08-26. If you can send a signed-ready term sheet and sample mapping today or tomorrow, we can move to legal review. If you have a DocuSign link for a preferred option that would speed things up.

Appreciate it,
Ava
VP Product Operations | HelioTech
ava@heliotech.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelioTech pricing alignment — procurement asks for fixed term + SKU mapping

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding procurement note from Ava (below). They want a contract-ready illustration, SKU 1:1 mapping, and a one-time onboarding credit ask (~$20k-$50k). Timeline is tight — they want vendor selection by 8/26.

My read:
- Timed credit gives us runway without long-term unit delta, but procurement hates variable credits in contracts. We can provide a schedule with caps (max credit amount) to make it palatable.
- SKU mapping is mostly ops work; engineering has already scoped typical mapping effort at ~8–12 hours to produce the sample mapping for their top 12 SKUs.
- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit; range depends on the concession ladder.

Proposed concession ladder (lean to protect ASP):
- Play A (preferred): Volume-tier: 18% baseline with tier boosts at 250M/500M tokens + $25k one-time onboarding credit; 12-month commit.
- Play B (compromise): Timed-credit schedule with explicit caps: $120k total credit pool available split across 9 months (caps defined in term sheet) + $30k onboarding credit; 9-month ramp; no change to unit ASP after credits.
- Play C (stretch): 22% blended discount at 12 months + $50k onboarding credit — only with leadership sign-off.

Operational asks: need legal to accept capped credit schedule language and product ops to commit to delivering SKU mapping within 3 business days. Also want to attach redwood-delta-term-sheet.pdf as the base.

Can you advise which play you want to approve? If we go Play B I can send a DocuSign-ready term sheet today.

—Karthik

On Aug 22, 2027, at 09:12 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Ava — great to connect earlier. As discussed, we ran two structured incentive approaches...

Attachments: redwood-delta-term-sheet.pdf (PDF)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioTech pricing alignment — procurement asks for fixed term + SKU mapping

Karthik / Marissa — I reviewed the ladder. Approve Play B as the commercial default for this deal. Rationale: keeps ASP protections, gives HelioTech perceivable near-term savings, and meets procurement preference for contractable caps.

Edits before sending:
- Cap the timed-credit pool at $120,000 (explicit schedule in term sheet).
- Offer onboarding credit at $30,000; position it as an implementation credit applied to first invoice rather than a cash rebate.
- Include a migration assistance clause: 40 hours SRE support at no charge to cover initial KV-cache tuning and model packaging.
- Do not auto-extend the credit pool beyond 9 months without a new signed amendment.

Once Karthik sends the DocuSign-ready Play B sheet I want a one-line exec approval included in the cover email for audit.

Lauren
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Final offer: capped timed-credit term sheet (Play B) — HelioTech

Ava — per procurement's ask and internal approvals, attached is the DocuSign-ready term sheet reflecting Play B: capped timed-credit pool + onboarding credit. Highlights below and the term sheet is attached as a PDF: redwood-delta-term-sheet.pdf. I also uploaded the 1:1 SKU mapping for your top 12 SKUs into the HubSpot record (link below).

Offer summary (Play B, contract-ready):
- Capped credit pool: $120,000 total, applied as a stepped credit across months 1–9. Schedule and per-invoice application rules are enumerated in Section 3 of the term sheet.
- Onboarding credit: $30,000 applied to first invoice as an implementation credit (not cash).
- Migration assistance: 40 hours SRE support included for KV-cache tuning, packaging, and runbook handoff.
- Standard 12-month invoice cadence; ASP returns to normal after credit pool exhaustion.
- No automatic extension of credit pool without signed amendment.

Action items for HelioTech procurement:
1) Review and sign the DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123
2) Confirm the committed initial monthly spend amount for the first 90 days so we can calendarize the tier gates in the mapping.
3) If you want the alternative (18% volume-tier with $25k onboarding) we can send that as a separate DocuSign option but it will need another round of legal review.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654321 (HLI-20270822-9)

We appreciate the tight timeline — happy to get on a short call after you sign to walk legal through the contract language.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
